O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Legitimate names must keep working: HEAD and one-level pseudo-refs, which ReferenceName.Validate rejects (rule 2, HEAD only special-cased), plus hierarchical names with dots inside components such as refs/heads/v1.2. Reusing Validate() as the fix, or a blanket '..' substring ban, breaks reading or writing these.

O7_producer.where: remote.go:307 (refspec Dst maps a remote-advertised name to a local ref name); also wire decoders plumbing/protocol/packp/updreq_decode.go:188 and packed-refs parser storage/filesystem/dotgit/dotgit.go:1311

O8b_injection_room.sibling: PackRefs deletes loose refs by joining ref.Name() into a path; a variant that also prunes names read from packed-refs would reach the remove sink unchecked
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: A maintainer could plausibly add 'prune stale loose refs listed in packed-refs' to PackRefs, and those names come from a file parser (dotgit.go:1311), not from the checked API.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: receive-pack accepts any command name; Command.validate only checks the action (plumbing/protocol/packp/updreq.go:75-81)
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: A server-side hook that writes per-ref state files (e.g. push certs or a lock file named after cmd.Name) is a natural feature that would reach a filesystem sink outside dotgit.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: the non-RW filesystem fallback setRefNorwfs is a second write implementation that receives fileName directly
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: If the check is placed in setRefRwfs rather than SetRef, the fallback for simple filesystems is left open, a classic second-implementation miss.
